# AIPerf — Python orchestrator + native runner session-bootstrap index

Single-page topology of the important source + design files, with a one-line
purpose for each, so an agent knows which file to open for a given question.

## ✅ Canonical / ⛔️ deprecated

- **CANONICAL PRODUCT PATH:** the Python `aiperf` CLI owns Config v2, planning,
  outer loops, and presentation; a fresh `aiperf-runner` child is the sole Rust
  executable and owns exactly one benchmark hot path. `crates/aiperf` is a
  runtime library and intentionally has no binary target.
- **DEPRECATED:** the `aiperf-rs` and `~/projects/aiperf-rust` trees (mechanical
  1:1 ports that reproduce the Python multiprocess/ZMQ complexity this design
  deletes). Do not build on them.
- **OWNERSHIP:** Rust execution truth is `crates/`; canonical Python frontend
  truth includes `src/aiperf/config`, `src/aiperf/orchestrator`, and
  `src/aiperf/cli_runner`. The old controller/service/ZMQ implementation under
  `src/` remains legacy and is not an alternate hot path.
- **Agent instructions:** `CLAUDE.md` = `AGENTS.md` = `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
  = `.cursor/rules/python.mdc` (byte-identical body; keep in sync via
  `python tools/check_agent_files_sync.py`).

## The architecture in one breath

Python resolves a run and sends a strict versioned request to
`aiperf-runner`. The runner drives **ONLINE-real** and **ONLINE-mock** over one
`{transport, clock}` seam. **OFFLINE-mock** is implemented behind the
`aiperf` library's non-default `dynamo-offline` feature, but runner protocol v1
does not expose it yet; it is not currently an AIPerf product mode.
Time lives behind `Clock` (`RealClock` vs
integer-ns DES `SimClock`); dispatch lives behind `RequestSink<R>` +
`RequestObserver` into a `TraceCollector`; token callbacks can carry
`ObservedTokenKind::{Output,Reasoning}` and fall back to unclassified `on_token`,
while terminal `ObservedUsage` carries endpoint counts as optional fields.
`is_virtual()` picks the `drive_real`
(reactor) vs `drive_sim` (idle-pump) driver over the *same* executor.
`RequestObserver` is intentionally local-loop (`!Send`/`!Sync`) so returned-event
fan-out and collection use `Rc`/`RefCell` without per-token locks. Thread-per-core,
`Rc`/`RefCell`, `!Send`, `spawn_local` on the hot path.

The complete canonical DynoSim/Mocker surface is also exposed through the Python
frontend: `aiperf dynosim {run,mocker,sweep,capabilities}`. `run` and `mocker`
forward raw argv to Dynamo's owning parsers; `sweep` calls the canonical four
`ReplayOptimizeSpec` search operations. The shipped capability manifest is
drift-checked against both argparse schemas, engine/router fields, Rust replay
exports, steppable methods, sweep models, and every Mocker Cargo feature.

## Crate topology (`crates/`)

| Crate | Read for | Entry files |
|---|---|---|
| `aiperf-clock` | the time seam: `Clock` trait, `SimClock` (int-ns DES heap, `(at_ns, seq_no)` tie-break), `RealClock` (`timerfd`/`AsyncFd`) | `src/clock.rs`, `src/sim_clock.rs`, `src/real_clock.rs` |
| `loadgen-core` | the dispatch/measure seam + report: `Dispatchable`, `RequestSink<R>`, local-loop `RequestObserver` (no `Send`/`Sync`; optional token classification; terminal usage with optional fields), `TraceCollector`, `TraceSimulationReport` | `src/sink.rs`, `src/collector.rs` |
| `aiperf-timing` | Clock-native scheduling + phase policy: arrivals, debt-draining slots, stop bounds, user-centric math, ramps, cancellation, URL selection, and `PhaseLifecycle`/`PhaseObserver`/`PhaseRunner`/`PhaseOrchestrator` with grace/drain/force escalation, seamless overlap, cancellation, and progress snapshots | `src/intervals.rs`, `src/slots.rs`, `src/stop.rs`, `src/user_centric.rs`, `src/ramping.rs`, `src/cancellation.rs`, `src/url_selection.rs`, `src/phase/` |
| `aiperf-adaptive` | transport-neutral adaptive-control leaf: live concurrency/prefill/rate/users actuators, tumbling windows joining arrival/admit/token/usage/terminal observations, authoritative completion-token OSL/ITL reconciliation, SLA evaluation, step policies, `ramp_until_fail` controller, Clock-paced runtime, schema-v2 artifacts | `src/actuator.rs`, `src/window.rs`, `src/sla.rs`, `src/step.rs`, `src/controller.rs`, `src/runtime.rs`, `src/artifacts.rs` |
| `aiperf-rng` | the hash-derived reproducibility leaf: `RngRoot::derive` + BLAKE3 seed derivation, canonical namespace constants, `RandomGenerator` (`Pcg64` + `rand_distr`), alloc-free `HashIdRandomGenerator`, generic `SamplingRng` / `DistributionSampler` / `SequenceSampler` seams, cached cumulative weighted distributions, fixed-seed profile canary | `src/derive.rs`, `src/namespace.rs`, `src/generator.rs`, `src/hash_id.rs`, `src/dist.rs` |
| `aiperf-dataset` | complete loader/composer/store/sampler/materializer pipeline: token-keyed prefix-dependent dense handles, exact raw/message replay, decoded HF + synthetic media, context reconstruction, sampler factories, tokenizer/fetch/request traits; accuracy carries only opaque evaluator correlation/task identity. `dag_jsonl` is a direct graph-program parser and is intentionally absent from the generic loader registry | `src/loader/`, `src/compose.rs`, `src/segment.rs`, `src/materialize.rs`, `src/request.rs`, `src/sampler.rs`, `src/tokenizer.rs`, `src/fetch.rs` |
| `aiperf-metrics` | IO-free performance/accuracy engine: validated 119-row catalog, NaN-sparse columns + exact ragged replay, record/aggregate/derived formulas, SLO/phase/window/timeslice logic, deterministic worker merge, effective/active/ICL sweeps, accuracy analysis, typed native-v2 reporter with exact static-evaluator and stateful agentic provenance/result blocks | `src/store.rs`, `src/accumulator.rs`, `src/sweepline/`, `src/catalog.rs`, `src/accuracy.rs`, `src/report.rs` |
| `aiperf-gpu-telemetry` | DCGM/Python GPU side-channel producer: parsing/scaling, exact boundary counters, cadence gauges, custom metrics, per-GPU summaries, and energy/power/efficiency joins | `src/source.rs`, `src/python_source.rs`, `src/parser.rs`, `src/fields.rs`, `src/collector.rs`, `src/accumulator.rs` |
| `aiperf-server-metrics` | Prometheus/OpenMetrics producer: routing/fallback/auto-disable, parser, exact counter/histogram boundaries, gauge distributions, histogram estimator, units, and vLLM/SGLang atlas | `src/source.rs`, `src/parser.rs`, `src/accumulator.rs`, `src/histogram.rs`, `src/atlas.rs`, `src/units.rs` |
| `aiperf-network-latency` | Fresh TCP-connect RTT calibration: target discovery, DNS fallback, Clock deadlines, nonfatal samples, per-target population stats, and flat-mean delivery | `src/probe.rs`, `src/accumulator.rs`, `src/model.rs` |
| `aiperf-accuracy` | versioned JSONL control plane: static `AccuracyEvaluator` plus stateful `AgenticEvaluator`, opaque problem/episode/call IDs, lossless agent/tool messages, provider-owned canonical agent configuration, generic/provider capabilities, callback configuration, and supervised long-lived `PythonEvaluator`; deliberately no Rust benchmark builders, graders, hidden-test decoder, code executor, dataset client, or dispatch path. | `src/protocol.rs`, `src/worker.rs` |
| `aiperf-extensions` | cycle-free compile-time composition: aggregate `AiperfRegistry`, transactional `AiperfExtension` application, and typed access to dataset-format, sampler, and the deterministic open endpoint-factory registry; accuracy is a directly injected process seam, not a Rust plugin category | `src/lib.rs` |
| `aiperf-core` | shared measurement helpers: OpenAI SSE chunk types, chat request-body builder, and `CollectorObserver` recorder; no HTTP client or clock of its own | `src/sse.rs`, `src/chat.rs`, `src/observer.rs` |
| `aiperf-endpoints` | trait-backed wire dialects plus the open registry foundation: validated `EndpointId`, co-located descriptors, identity-free raw/effective policy, deterministic factories/aliases, dense worker-local prepared bindings, readiness policy, and compile-once raw/template state. Protocol-v1 enum/metadata remain compatibility-only | `src/registry.rs`, `src/config.rs`, `src/anthropic.rs`, `src/endpoints.rs`, `src/tier2/flexible.rs`, `tests/registry.rs` |
| `aiperf-transport` | the Clock-injected hyper transport (h1/h2c/UDS, rustls, fine-grained trace timing, meaningful-SSE first-token filtering, captured full-body send completion, post-send HTTP 499 cancellation, reuse strategies) | `src/client/`, `src/transport/`, `src/sse/`, `src/models/` |
| `aiperf-graph` | Backend-neutral Graph-IR dataflow over the unified segment store, direct authored-input adapter registry + canonical lowering, trait-backed root/arrival/admission/placement/failure policy, firing-gate executor, clock-only and external-source DES drivers, transport benches, and worker-local native metrics merged once at join | `src/input.rs`, `src/lowering.rs`, `src/workload.rs`, `src/placement.rs`, `src/runtime.rs`, `src/executor.rs`, `src/materialize.rs`, `src/transport_bench.rs` |
| `aiperf-runner` | sole strict Rust executable: v1 online execution plus exact-image-bound strict-v2 bootstrap/static validation, frozen endpoint/backend/workload capability registries, executable-only pair inventory, endpoint selection (including `messages`), scheduled phases, direct online `dag_jsonl` Graph-IR, native HTTP, static accuracy, adaptive controls, live events, telemetry sidecars, request artifacts, metric joins, and native-v2 result | `src/main.rs`, `src/protocol_v2.rs`, `src/registry.rs`, `src/execute.rs`, `src/graph_execution.rs`, `src/protocol.rs`, `src/gpu_telemetry.rs`, `src/server_metrics.rs`, `src/network_latency.rs` |
| `aiperf` | library-only load-generation runtime composed by `aiperf-runner`: online paced/scheduled/adaptive/static-accuracy paths plus retained stateful-agentic and feature-gated offline implementations. Agentic and offline are not runner-reachable yet. | `src/agentic.rs`, `src/agentic_gateway.rs`, `src/dynamo_offline.rs`, `src/phase_runtime.rs`, `src/ancillary.rs`, `src/metrics.rs`, `src/accuracy.rs`, `src/adaptive.rs`, `src/run.rs`, `src/request_rate.rs`, `src/scheduled.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`, `src/user_centric.rs`, `src/fixed_schedule.rs`, `src/report.rs` |

Deps: `aiperf` → {`aiperf-accuracy`, `aiperf-adaptive`, `aiperf-core`,
`aiperf-dataset`, `aiperf-graph`, `aiperf-metrics`, `aiperf-timing`,
`aiperf-transport`, `aiperf-clock`, `loadgen-core`} plus optional
`dynamo-mocker` only under `dynamo-offline`; `aiperf-extensions` →
{`aiperf-dataset`, `aiperf-endpoints`}; `aiperf-accuracy` has no workspace-crate dependency;
`aiperf-adaptive` → {`aiperf-clock`, `aiperf-metrics`,
`aiperf-timing`, `loadgen-core`}; `aiperf-dataset` → {`aiperf-clock`,
`aiperf-endpoints`, `aiperf-rng`, `aiperf-transport`}; `aiperf-graph` → {`aiperf-core`, `aiperf-dataset`,
`aiperf-metrics`, `aiperf-timing`, `aiperf-transport`, `aiperf-clock`,
`loadgen-core`}; `aiperf-timing` → {`aiperf-clock`, `aiperf-rng`};
`aiperf-core` → `loadgen-core`; `aiperf-transport` →
`aiperf-clock`. `aiperf-metrics` stays IO-free and runtime-neutral.

Telemetry deps: `aiperf-runner` composes all three leaves;
`aiperf-gpu-telemetry` and `aiperf-server-metrics` → {`aiperf-clock`,
`aiperf-metrics`, `aiperf-transport`}; `aiperf-network-latency` →
{`aiperf-clock`, `aiperf-metrics`}. Core metrics never depends back on a producer.

## Run AIPerf

```bash
# Generate, validate, and run through the only user-facing entry point.
aiperf config init --template minimal --output benchmark.yaml
aiperf config validate benchmark.yaml
aiperf profile --config benchmark.yaml

# Developer-only runner protocol inventory; normal runs are launched by Python.
cargo run --release -p aiperf-runner -- --capabilities
```

`cargo run -p aiperf` is intentionally invalid: the `aiperf` Rust package has
no binary. Config-v2 YAML expresses endpoints, datasets, phases, ramps,
cancellation, adaptive policy, accuracy, telemetry, artifacts, and open
backend/workload selections. Python expands outer loops; execution retains the
protocol-v1 compatibility projection while a side-effect-free authored-v2
projection is available for validation and contract tests.

The online concurrency and request-rate issuers own all applicable live ramp
actuators. User-centric owns only its optional session-concurrency pool, while
fixed schedule owns none; unsupported ramps fail validation rather than becoming
inert. Scheduled strategies support per-turn cancellation and turn-zero sticky
endpoint routing.

## Canonical static accuracy

Static accuracy is configured through Config v2 and launched by
`aiperf profile --config ...`. Python selects the pinned evaluator environment;
the runner supervises it while retaining all inference traffic and timing.

Rust sends every LLM request and parses every response through its normal
transport. The Python/Lighteval child prepares opaque problems and batch-grades
terminal response text; it never contacts the inference server, and ground
truth/private tests never cross the JSONL protocol. Protocol v1 rejects unknown
static-response fields and restricts static prompts to `{role, content}`; stateful
agent/tool messages retain role-specific fields losslessly. The worker redirects
ambient fd 1 output to stderr and native v2 records its source/lock identity.

## Stateful agentic accuracy — library built, runner work remaining

The Harbor, AgentLab/BrowserGym, and MCPMark providers and Rust
`AgenticWorkload` remain implemented, but runner protocol v1 has no stateful
episode/callback request. After native CLI removal there is no end-user agentic
path. Restore it only through a versioned runner DTO plus real runner subprocess
canaries; do not add a second CLI or move model traffic into Python.

Harbor owns task packages, Terminus-2, environments, trajectories, terminal
execution, and verifier rewards. Primary calls use its queue callback. Packaged
LLM-backed environments/verifiers receive an authenticated callback address;
Rust's ingress converts those calls to the same scheduled workload and never
forwards directly. Rust issues every turn through the generic online
scheduled/transport runner. Native v2 records exact worker/lock/container,
harness source/version, dataset revision, agent, environment, verifier, authored
configuration, canonical rewards, episode records, and artifacts. Infrastructure
and cancellation records are never converted into zero/incorrect scores.
Harbor's canonical source forms are accepted unchanged: Hub
`org/name@ref`, legacy `name@version` (for example `bfcl@1.0`), and an existing
local task-directory path. Hub tags are reported as resolved content hashes;
legacy versions are frozen before Harbor enumerates their tasks.

The former native-CLI Harbor, BrowserGym, and MCPMark live canaries were
deleted with that unreachable product route. Focused library tests still prove
normal scheduled transport and callback accounting.

AgentLab 0.4.2 plus BrowserGym 0.14.3 is the canonical browser provider. It
directly runs `DEFAULT_BENCHMARKS`, `GenericAgent`, and `ExpArgs`; its sync model
callback emits JSONL and only a Rust terminal result can resume the browser
loop. BrowserGym owns prompts, actions, Playwright transitions, traces, and
rewards. Browser tasks use dependency-safe sequential admission. The separately
hashed worker lock is required because AgentLab's OpenAI <2 constraint conflicts
with Harbor's LiteLLM/OpenAI 2.x constraint.

MCPMark commit `cd45b7f57923b9b3985467f5139927575f83141c` is a third
independently hash-locked provider. MCPMark owns the registry, task instructions,
100-turn loop, MCP servers, state managers, task-local `verify.py`, artifacts,
and cleanup. AIPerf replaces only `litellm.acompletion` with its JSONL broker;
Python never receives a model-server URL. Native v2 records MCPMark's exact
source/lock, canonical agent controls, selected server artifact, task digest,
and concrete local-environment digest.

## Run the scheduled workloads

Request-rate, concurrency, user-centric, and fixed-schedule strategies are
Config-v2 phase variants executed by the runner. See
`src/aiperf/config/templates/{latency_test,multi_turn_conversation,fixed_schedule}.yaml`
for runnable examples.

Fixed-trace zero/window policy is expressed in the Config-v2 fixed-schedule
phase. Rust records scheduled, issued, dispatch, first-token, TTFT, terminal,
and aggregate lateness facts in the native result/artifacts selected by Python.

## AIPerf offline engine — library built, runner work remaining

The workspace root expects `../../../dynamo-aiperf-native`. Library developers
can compile the adapter; `dynamo-full` enables every optional mocker family:

```bash
cargo build -p aiperf --features dynamo-offline
cargo test -p aiperf --features dynamo-offline --lib
```

There is no native `--offline` CLI and runner protocol v1 has no offline
backend DTO. The adapter is therefore not an AIPerf end-user mode until it is
lowered through the runner with the full parity/fail-closed test matrix.

Single, aggregate, and disaggregate topologies, both routers, all five trace
formats, cancellation, ramps, adaptive controls, SLA goodput, and raw/timed
artifacts run on one `SimClock` with no inference server. Before any offline API
returns, the complete common flat reports must serialize to identical compact
JSON bytes: 74 base fields, plus three goodput fields when configured. Requested
KV offload fails closed on initialization error. Canonical accuracy alone remains
online because the timing engine does not generate semantic answer text.

## Run the complete canonical DynoSim/Mocker frontend

```bash
aiperf dynosim run trace.jsonl --replay-mode offline --report-json replay.json
aiperf dynosim mocker --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --endpoint dynamo.Mocker
aiperf dynosim sweep optimize.yaml --operation compare_topologies --output sweep.json
aiperf dynosim capabilities
```

These commands require an ai-dynamo Python installation. `run` and `mocker`
delegate to the canonical implementations, so their calculations and artifacts
are the same implementation—not an AIPerf reimplementation.

## "Which file answers…" quick map

- **How is virtual time deterministic?** `crates/aiperf-clock/src/sim_clock.rs`
  (min-heap, `(at_ns, seq_no)`, `advance_to`) + `aiperf-graph/src/runtime.rs`
  (`drive_sim` and `drive_sim_with_source` idle-pumps).
- **How is a request dispatched + measured?** `loadgen-core/src/sink.rs` (traits)
  → `aiperf/src/http.rs` (`TransportSink`) →
  `aiperf-core/src/observer.rs` (`CollectorObserver`).
- **Where is accuracy ownership split?** `aiperf-accuracy/src/{protocol,worker}.rs`
  (static + stateful supervised evaluator seams) → `src/aiperf/accuracy/{worker,agentic,model_broker,harbor,harbor_agent,browsergym,mcpmark}.py`
  (canonical Python task/agent/environment/verifier ownership) and
  `aiperf/src/accuracy.rs` (normal Rust static dataset lowering, response capture,
  batched grade correlation, accumulation/reporting) or `aiperf/src/agentic.rs`
  (stateful Rust admission, normal-pipeline model-call issuance, and typed
  native-v2 result composition), plus `aiperf/src/agentic_gateway.rs` (authenticated
  environment/verifier OpenAI ingress with no inference client). Runner protocol
  support for the stateful path is still missing.
- **Where do native TTFT/ITL/e2e/throughput/goodput and sweeps come from?**
  `aiperf/src/metrics.rs` (runtime join) → `aiperf-metrics/src/{store,accumulator,sweepline}.rs`.
  `aiperf/src/http.rs` also translates the real transport trace into HTTP metric facts;
  `loadgen-core/src/collector.rs` remains the compact compatibility summary.
- **Where are streamed chunks and usage parsed?** `aiperf-core/src/sse.rs`
  (`ChatChunk`, `Usage`) + `aiperf-core/src/observer.rs` (delta-token recorder).
  Usage reconciliation to authoritative token counts is not yet reimplemented.
- **How does the online loop work?** `aiperf/src/run.rs` (Clock-paced arrival
  generator, dynamic session/prefill `SlotPool`s, `StopChecker`, adaptive task).
- **How do user-centric and fixed-schedule runs work?**
  `aiperf/src/{scheduled,scheduler,user_centric,fixed_schedule,multiturn}.rs`;
  exact virtual-time coverage is in `aiperf/tests/scheduled_sim.rs`, and real HTTP
  library timing coverage is in `aiperf/tests/scheduled_real_mock.rs`.
- **How does adaptive scale work?** `aiperf-adaptive/src/{window,sla,step,controller,runtime}.rs`
  (pure control) → `aiperf/src/adaptive.rs` (live-actuator assembly) →
  `aiperf/src/run.rs` (backend-neutral online/offline issuer integration).
- **Where do ramps, request cancellation, and sticky endpoint selection live?**
  `aiperf-timing/src/{ramping,cancellation,url_selection}.rs` (policy traits) →
  `aiperf/src/{ancillary,run,scheduled,http}.rs` (issuer/session wiring) →
  `aiperf-transport/src/{client,transport}/` (send-complete abort).
- **How does authored DAG input reach graph mode directly?**
  `aiperf-graph/src/input.rs` (adapter registry + complete-source parse) →
  `lowering.rs` (`GraphTracePlan` + frozen `SegmentStore`, no linear dataset) →
  `workload.rs` / `placement.rs` → `aiperf-runner/src/graph_execution.rs`.
  The throughput harness remains `aiperf-graph/src/transport_bench.rs`
  (thread-per-core lanes, aiperf-transport, UDS).
- **How are prompts built without re-serializing?** `aiperf-dataset/src/segment.rs`
  (blake3 prefix-dependent dense handles) + `materialize.rs` (wire splice).
- **Where is native-v2 JSON built/written?** `aiperf-metrics/src/report.rs` →
  `aiperf/src/report.rs`; strict run selection/composition is in
  `aiperf-runner/src/{protocol,execute}.rs`.

## Design specs (`specs/` — intent, not code)

Full index + status (decided / sketch / superseded): [`specs/README.md`](specs/README.md).

- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-port-exact-vs-redo-ledger.md` — **read first**:
  scope rulings + the credit-policy trap + the three-modes framing. Addendum:
  online/offline parity is shared code path + report schema, not byte-identical values.
- `specs/2026-07-10-shared-rust-architecture-northstar.md` — the target
  abstraction (aspirational vocabulary); its latest addendum replaces the
  native App/CLI layer with Python Config v2 plus the strict runner.
- `specs/2026-07-10-steppable-clock-injected-engine-design.md` — **library built
  behind `dynamo-offline`; runner projection pending**: neutral two-source DES pump,
  in-process sink/observer/completion/cancellation seam, all profiles/topologies/
  routers/trace formats, paced/scheduled/graph consumers, SLA/raw/timed artifacts,
  AIC/offload feature families, and byte-exact no-server conformance against the
  sibling Dynamo mocker. The runner-only execution-surface spec owns the pending
  feature-gated product projection.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-transport-rust-port-design.md` — the Clock-injected
  hyper transport (→ `aiperf-transport`).
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-dataset-segment-seam-design.md` — **built end to
  end + addenda** as `aiperf-dataset`: full loader→compose→dense
  store→sampler→materializer flow shared by the runner, accuracy, and Graph-IR,
  including exact replay, decoded/synthetic media, context/dispatch fields, and
  opaque accuracy correlation/task ids; direct `dag_jsonl` bypasses linear
  `Dataset`/`Conversation`/`DagMetadata` composition. Rust no longer stores
  evaluator ground truth.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-compile-time-extension-registry-design.md` —
  **built + addenda** statically linked replacement for `plugins.yaml`:
  aggregate transactional registration for dataset formats, samplers, and
  endpoints. Accuracy benchmark/grader categories are deleted in favor of the
  directly injected Python-worker evaluator seam. The endpoint addendum points
  to the runner-owned redesign for open dialect IDs and production composition.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-runner-owned-endpoint-registry-design.md` —
  **foundation + v2 capability/validation convergence built; execution convergence pending + addenda; authoritative for endpoint ownership**:
  `aiperf-endpoints` owns open IDs, adapter-local descriptors, deterministic factory/alias
  composition, raw/effective configuration, worker-local prepared bindings/dense keys,
  readiness policy, and compile-once raw/template state; `aiperf-extensions` proves a genuinely
  new dialect. Runner capability and v2 static-validation paths now consume the frozen registry;
  protocol-v1 execution compatibility authorities and prepared-binding convergence remain. The addendum also
  pins authored preflight, completeness, the strict v2 envelope, and exact image identity;
  mode reachability is intentionally delegated to the next spec.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-runner-only-execution-surface-design.md` — **decided /
  v2 bootstrap and static validation built; pair execution pending; authoritative for native product reachability**: one strict image-bound v2
  runner envelope composes registered `online_http` or feature-gated
  `dynamo_offline` backends with scheduled, Graph-IR, static-accuracy, or
  stateful-agentic workloads. The decoder, typed terminals, factory-owned strict config decode,
  registry-derived static compatibility, and executable-only `supported_pairs` are built; pair
  preparation/execution, native-v2, packaging, migration, and subprocess gates remain per pair.
  Direct online `dag_jsonl` Graph-IR is already product-reachable through the
  protocol-v1 compatibility projection.
- `specs/2026-07-11-python-orchestrator-rust-single-run-design.md` — **built v1 +
  authored v2 static validation; v2 pair execution pending**: Python `aiperf` is the only human frontend
  and `aiperf-runner` the only Rust executable. Python owns structural Config v2 and
  outer/presentation loops; the authored v2 request avoids resolved state and side
  effects. Rust now owns strict image-bound static validation; the separate execution-surface spec owns pair preparation and
  the remaining offline/agentic projections; direct online `dag_jsonl` Graph-IR is
  runner-reachable through protocol v1.
- `specs/2026-07-10-unified-graph-runtime-design.md` — **the realization design**:
  every load mode reduces to one dispatch verb on the clock-scheduled graph
  executor; strategies become `Workload` schedule generators. Supersedes the
  scheduling sketch; addendum maps old RNG wording to BLAKE3 and translates
  north-star seam names to current `RequestSink` / `RequestObserver` symbols.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-scheduling-policy-sketch.md` — early `Scheduler`
  sketch for credit *policy*. **Superseded by the unified-graph-runtime design's**
  `Workload` / `SlotPool` / `RatePool` / `Gate` seams.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-request-rate-multiturn-design.md` — **built +
  implementation addendum**: `RequestRateWorkload` is the source-grounded
  single-loop issuer emitting one turn per interval (FIFO continuation-priority,
  NOT conversation arrivals), with session + prefill `SlotPool`s, TTFT/terminal
  release, `StopChecker` bounds, segment-pool materialization, and Clock-deferred
  think time. Synthetic and dataset runner paths share `ScheduledRuntime`; exact
  `SimClock`, real-HTTP, and feature-gated Dynamo tests pin policy and reply splicing.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-user-centric-fixed-schedule-design.md` — **built +
  addendum**: shared Clock-backed `ScheduledRuntime`, conversation/scheduler/source/
  workload traits, user-centric steady-state seeding + churn + continuation pacing,
  and fixed absolute trace replay are wired through Config v2 and the runner. Exact `SimClock`
  and real `aiperf-mock-rs` library tests plus runner tests validate ordering,
  drain, timing, TTFT, and reply splicing.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-phase-runner-orchestrator-design.md` — **built +
  implementation addendum**: validated lifecycle/config/progress, direct observers,
  Clock-driven timeout/grace/cancel/drain/force escalation, failure finalization,
  ordered warmup→profiling execution, seamless overlap, and shared-slot debt drain live
  in `aiperf-timing::phase`; `aiperf::phase_runtime` connects scheduled workloads,
  phase-owned ramps, processors, `SimClock`, and real HTTP. Config v2 and runner
  protocol v1 author ordered warmup/profiling lists. Direct Graph-IR executes a
  narrower `GraphWorkload` phase policy; full `PhaseLifecycle` integration remains.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-adaptive-scale-design.md` — **built + addendum**:
  `aiperf-adaptive` implements the actuator/evaluator/step/window/controller traits,
  Python-grounded SLA math with authoritative completion-token OSL/ITL reconciliation,
  Clock-paced `ramp_until_fail`, and schema-v2 artifacts;
  online and feature-gated offline modes share the injected-backend futures for
  paced concurrency/prefill, scheduled request rate, and user-centric target users.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-ancillary-timing-policy-design.md` — **built +
  addendum**: Clock-driven Linear/Exponential/Poisson ramps, seeded warmup-aware
  Bernoulli fixed-delay policy, full-body send-complete HTTP 499 cancellation,
  and turn-zero round-robin with sticky session routing are implemented and
  wired into online issuers. Config v2 and runner phase DTOs expose applicable ramps,
  cancellation, and endpoint selection; the addendum records the exact workload support
  matrix and remaining companion phase/graph consumers.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-dag-branch-orchestrator-design.md` — **superseded by the
  `aiperf-graph` async-dataflow engine**: FORK/SPAWN fan-out = out-edges, join =
  `ChannelRequirement.count`, sticky-routing/drain-observer = deleted credit-protocol
  artifacts. Direct lowering, FORK/SPAWN materialization, whole-trace session/static-
  node bounds, and FAIL_FAST are built for runner `dag_jsonl`. Lineage doc.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-coverage-gap-ledger.md` — research synthesis of
  unspec'd bodies; addendum notes metrics, telemetry, and RNG gaps are now covered
  by dedicated specs/addenda.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-accuracy-accumulator-design.md` — **static
  accuracy built in runner; agentic library built / runner pending + addenda**:
  Rust owns inference/timing/metrics/reporting and supervised pinned Python
  workers own canonical datasets, environments, hidden tests, loops, and scoring.
  Static Lighteval is runner subprocess-tested. Harbor, AgentLab/BrowserGym, and
  MCPMark remain library/provider implementations; the runner-only execution-surface
  spec owns their pending strict workload/callback projection and restored process canaries.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-metrics-accumulator-sweepline-design.md` — **built +
  addenda**: columnar/ragged engine, formulas/SLOs, full effective/active/ICL sweeps,
  duration-weighted stats, windows/timeslices, worker merge, all-mode runtime wiring,
  and native-v2 `Reporter`; built telemetry remains a separate consumer and v1
  compatibility remains unbuilt.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-metric-catalog-appendix.md` — **built + addendum**:
  103 inherited metric identities plus 16 sweep identities, exact metadata/formulas,
  dependency validation and fingerprint; GPU energy and network-adjusted rows inject
  when their optional producers are enabled.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-telemetry-accumulators-design.md` — **built + addenda**:
  `aiperf-gpu-telemetry`, `aiperf-server-metrics`, and `aiperf-network-latency`
  implement the shared side-channel accumulator seam; `aiperf-runner` owns their
  Clock-paced tasks, exact phase snapshots, finalize-order energy/network joins,
  native server report blocks, compatibility JSONL, fallback/auto-disable state
  machine, vLLM/SGLang atlas, histogram estimator, and TCP calibration.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-exporters-overhaul-design.md` — **partially built +
  addenda**: native-v2 typed reporter + runner JSON writer are built. The removed
  Rust CLI's tables, accuracy CSV, logger, and legacy writers are deleted; Python
  owns presentation. General metric CSV, genai-perf-v1 compatibility, warnings,
  console replay, and uploaders remain unbuilt in Rust.
- `specs/2026-07-11-aiperf-rust-endpoints-design.md` — **built + implementation
  addendum**: every tier-1 and tier-2 dialect is implemented behind the faithful
  `Endpoint` trait, including raw/template JMESPath + Jinja and input-side ISL accounting.
  Multipart, Clock-paced polling/download, inline-media retrieval/deduplication, endpoint
  streaming paths, and lifecycle-wide post-send cancellation live in `aiperf-transport`;
  real-loopback tests cover the dialect families, wire lifecycles, and native modality metrics.
  Its endpoint-identity/registry/config-ownership claims are superseded by the runner-owned
  endpoint-registry spec; its formatting/parsing/replay behavior remains authoritative.
- `specs/2026-07-10-aiperf-rust-rng-derive-system-design.md` — the hash-derived
  RNG substrate: `blake3(f"{root}:{id}")[:8]`→u64 order-independent seed derivation
  + canonical namespace constants + `HashIdRandomGenerator` (per-`(trace_id,
  hash_id)` reseed) + `RandomGenerator` and generic sampler contracts; ruling: NO
  cross-language byte parity — one deterministic PRNG (`Pcg64`) + `rand_distr`
  with faithful distribution/edge-case semantics; internal reproducibility +
  order-independence (lock-free per-thread, alloc-free reseed). Built as leaf crate
  `aiperf-rng`; a Rust-internal fixed-seed profile canary pins the stream. Dataset
  composition/samplers and ancillary timing policies consume it; broader
  scheduler/graph integration remains.
- `specs/2026-07-09-graph-ir-rust-port-design.md` — Graph-IR runtime plus direct
  authored `dag_jsonl` lowering are built in `aiperf-graph`; addenda supersede
  standalone/offline-only framing with the current `LocalSet` +
  `drive_sim`/`drive_real` + HTTP-dispatch path and assign product reachability to
  the runner-only `graph` workload.
- `specs/2026-07-09-dynamo-aiperf-{shared-core,request-rate-tokenizer}-design.md`
  — historical precursors (built on dynamo's `lib/mocker`; superseded by the
  standalone workspace).

## Build / test / run

Use `cargo build --release`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, and
`cargo fmt` for Rust development. Build the optional library adapter with
`cargo build -p aiperf --features dynamo-offline`. End users run
`aiperf profile --config benchmark.yaml`; Python launches `aiperf-runner`.
`cargo run -p aiperf` and native `--offline`/mode flags do not exist.
